items.claim: The row's opening-seam denial suppresses the chapter's only contiguous ruach catchword pair, and its cross-row root note cites the divergent site while omitting the identical-form one.
items.evidence: Skeleton sweep of the ruach root over chapter 7 returns exactly 2 verses (unit: verses) and they are adjacent: oshb:Eccl.7.8 carries two tokens, “ט֥וֹב אֶֽרֶךְ ר֖וּחַ מִגְּבַהּ רֽוּחַ” (byte tier), and the row's own verse carries the suffixed “בְּרֽוּחֲךָ֖” (byte tier). Object named to avoid the resh-ayin blend: neither ch-7 token belongs to the reut-ruach set (7 verses) or the rayon-ruach set (2 verses) — no ch-7 member in either, so this is the bare ruach lexeme in its temperament sense in both verses. That is a byte-true lexeme straddling the row's own opening seam, and it argues continuity against the split; the row discloses no ruach signal and asserts instead that the verse shares nothing with the saying before it, a claim that holds only at phrase level and is not qualified as such. Second defect, engagement class: device_notes makes a root claim about “be hasty” recurring at web:Eccl.8.3 “in a different stem” with NO quoted pointed form at either site, and the staged extract carries no morphology layer with which a stem claim can be settled. The root sweep returns exactly 3 verses book-wide (unit: verses) — oshb:Eccl.5.1 (= web:Eccl.5.2), oshb:Eccl.7.9, oshb:Eccl.8.3. The one the row cites is the divergent one, “אַל תִּבָּהֵ֤ל” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.8.3); the one it omits is the exact match — “אַל תְּבַהֵ֨ל” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.5.1 = web:Eccl.5.2, offset zone) against the row's own “אַל תְּבַהֵ֥ל” (byte tier). An incomplete root sweep that drops its closest parallel, and drops it inside the offset zone, cannot carry the cross-row echo it is offered for.

items.claim: The row's explicit statement that this verse anticipates the following pair “without sharing their vocabulary” is refuted by its own bytes: the wisdom lexeme is shared straight across the row's closing seam.
items.evidence: The wisdom root (het-kaf-mem, swept as a bound root, NOT the contained-substring kaf-mem-he class whose 22 hits are 22/22 false) returns 7 verses in chapter 7 (unit: verses): 7:4, 7:10, 7:11, 7:12, 7:19, 7:23, 7:25 — and 7:10/7:11/7:12 are a contiguous three-verse chain. The row's own verse ends “כִּ֛י לֹ֥א מֵחָכְמָ֖ה שָׁאַ֥לְתָּ עַל זֶֽה” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.10); the immediately following verse opens “טוֹבָ֥ה חָכְמָ֖ה עִֽם נַחֲלָ֑ה” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.11); the verse after that carries “הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה” twice (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.12, 2 tokens). So the shared item is not an English-side anticipation of a theme, it is the same lexeme in three consecutive verses. The claim is load-bearing — it is the stated reason this verse stays atomic rather than joining the wisdom-value pair — and it is byte-false. It is also inconsistent with the cluster's own standard one row later, where “both verses share the root” of exactly this lexeme is offered as merge-grade cohesion binding 7:11 to 7:12; the identical evidence at identical strength reaches back into 7:10 and is here declared absent. Separately, the row's device note “No tov-opener or refrain tag” is true only of the opener slot: the verse carries the comparative “הָי֥וּ טוֹבִ֖ים מֵאֵ֑לֶּה” (byte tier), a contiguous tov-plus-min adjacency that the staged adjacency list (6 verses) does not capture because it is plural-inflected — exactly the phrase-extension trap — so the chapter's better-than texture does run through this verse, undisclosed.

items.claim: The internal merge is byte-sound and the offset-zone crosswalk checks out, but the row's opening-seam denial of shared vocabulary is byte-false and one cited Hebrew form is below quotation tier.
items.evidence: Credit where the bytes give it: both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier against their cited refs; the shared-root claim is true — “חָכְמָ֖ה” (oshb:Eccl.7.11) and “הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה” twice (oshb:Eccl.7.12), byte tier; the tov-opener ordinal is right (the staged inventory lists 12 openers book-wide, 7 in this chapter, and 7:11 is the 6th); and the dual is both arithmetically and CONTENTFULLY correct — oshb:Eccl.5.8 does carry “וְיִתְר֥וֹן אֶ֖רֶץ בַּכֹּ֣ל” (byte tier), so the yitron reference lands on the right verse rather than reading MT ch-5 bytes under a same-numbered WEB ref. The challenge: the row states the pair is “held apart from the nostalgia admonition before it (no shared vocabulary)” while the preceding verse carries “מֵחָכְמָ֖ה” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.10) — the same lexeme the row itself makes the pair's binding evidence one clause earlier. The wisdom-root sweep gives a contiguous 7:10-7:11-7:12 chain (7 verses in the chapter, unit: verses), so the opening seam is asserted against the row's own operative criterion. Second, the particle cited in prose as proof the second verse “does not stand alone” re-collates at accent_stripped, not byte, against oshb:Eccl.7.12, whose source form is “כִּ֛י” — a hand-typed pointed run below quotation grade and carrying no tier label. Third, the row's own first verse ends on “לְרֹאֵ֥י הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ” (byte tier), one of the 5 bare-shemesh verses outside the under-the-sun formula (unit: verses) — correctly NOT claimed as the refrain, but undisclosed, and the same root recurs as the imperative at 7:13 and 7:14 just past the row's closing seam.

items.claim: The pair's binding evidence sits outside every quoted run, the second quote overruns its own gloss by one token, and the closing seam carries an undisclosed same-root straddle.
items.evidence: The row binds the two verses on the shared “made/work” root with God as subject, but neither quoted run contains the token that would show it: the quote of the second verse stops at “רְאֵ֑ה גַּ֣ם” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.14) while the token doing the work, “עָשָׂ֣ה הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים” (byte tier, same verse), is left unquoted. That truncation also breaks quote/gloss parity: the Hebrew run carries one token past the curly-quoted WEB run, which stops at “consider” and never renders that particle. The subject description is imprecise at the first verse: the token there is the construct “מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.13), where the divine name is the nomen rectum of a construct chain, not a subject — only the second verse has it as verbal subject. The root is also not seam-exclusive: the chapter-7 sweep returns 4 verses (unit: verses) — 7:13, 7:14, 7:20, 7:29 — so it recurs inside another row of this same cluster. Finally the closing seam: the row's own imperative “רְאֵ֑ה” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.14) is answered across the seam by “רָאִ֖יתִי” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.15), the same root the row makes binding evidence inside its own span, and the adjacent resh-ayin pair “רָעָ֖ה” / “בְּרָעָתֽוֹ” (byte tier; ch-7 sweep 3 verses — 7:3, 7:14, 7:15 — objects split, calamity vs evildoing, not blended) straddles it too. Neither is disclosed. The row's strongest byte-true tie goes uncited: both verses take the DEFINITE divine form (28 definite verses vs 7 bare, unit: verses), which is the form-level evidence the pairing actually rests on.

items.claim: The verse is isolated on a register shift while four byte-true lexical chains straddle its two seams undisclosed, and the hevel-family token inside its own bytes is not disclosed at all.
items.evidence: Opening seam: “רָאִ֖יתִי” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.15) shares its root with the imperative “רְאֵ֑ה” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.14) immediately before it — the very root the preceding row of this cluster cites as binding evidence — and “בְּרָעָתֽוֹ” answers “רָעָ֖ה” (byte tier; chapter-7 resh-ayin sweep 3 verses, unit: verses, objects split: calamity at 7:14 vs evildoing at 7:15, not blended). Closing seam: the paradox's two nouns are redeployed in the very verses of the following row — “צַדִּיק֙” (oshb:Eccl.7.15) recurs as “צַדִּיק֙” (oshb:Eccl.7.16) and “רָשָׁ֔ע” (oshb:Eccl.7.15) recurs in “אַל תִּרְשַׁ֥ע הַרְבֵּ֖ה” (oshb:Eccl.7.17), all byte tier; chapter-7 sweeps give 3 verses each (7:15, 7:16, 7:20 and 7:15, 7:17, 7:25; unit: verses). The row argues this relation only in English (“the counsel responds to”) and never discloses it as byte-true shared lexemes, which is precisely the cross-seam cohesion that argues continuity against the split. Third: the verse carries “בִּימֵ֣י הֶבְלִ֑י” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.15) — the suffixed hevel form, which is the SOLE book occurrence of that spelling and one of only 2 hevel-family tokens in this chapter (the other at oshb:Eccl.7.6); the family runs 38 tokens over 30 verses book-wide, and suffixed forms like this one escape bare-token sweeps entirely. The row's substrate signals name only the I-saw frame. That citation is itself correct (the staged inventory lists this verse among 18 I-saw verses, unit: verses, object named) — credited.

items.claim: Two stated grounds are refuted by the row's own closing verse: it declares no tov-opener or refrain token in the span when its last verse IS a tov-opener, and it claims the unit resolves on a positive imperative when that verse carries a third negative imperative it declines to quote.
items.evidence: The row's substrate signal reads “no tov-opener or refrain token in this span (imperative frame instead)”. oshb:Eccl.7.18 opens “ט֚וֹב אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֶּאֱחֹ֣ז בָּזֶ֔ה” (byte tier) and is listed in the staged device inventory as a tov-opener — 12 openers book-wide, 7 of them in this chapter (7:1, 7:2, 7:3, 7:5, 7:8, 7:11, 7:18; unit: verses, object: verses whose first token is tov/tovah). The cluster's own 7:11-7:12 row cites its verse as “6th of 7 in-chapter sites”, so the 7th site is exactly the verse this row says carries none; the WEB witness opens it the same way. Since a verse-initial tov is the chapter's own dominant seam-marker, the signal is not merely absent, it points AGAINST closing the unit on that verse. Second: the row states the counsel “resolves on a positive imperative rather than another negation”, but the same verse carries “וְגַם מִזֶּ֖ה אַל תַּנַּ֣ח אֶת יָדֶ֑ךָ” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.18) — a third al-plus-jussive negation, in the span, omitted from the quoted run; the WEB witness renders it too. Third, the run the row does quote, “כִּֽי יְרֵ֥א אֱלֹהִ֖ים” (byte tier), is not an imperative form at all — the row's own gloss renders it substantivally — so the “positive imperative” description has no byte referent anywhere in the verse. Two further undisclosed signals in the same verse: it is this chapter's ONLY fear-root site (8 verses book-wide, unit: verses) and one of just 7 bare-divine-name verses against 28 definite ones — a form split that distinguishes it from the two definite forms two rows earlier. Finally the span's middle verse carries no quoted Hebrew although the “two negative imperatives” claim is a Hebrew-form claim; its form is “אַל תִּרְשַׁ֥ע הַרְבֵּ֖ה וְאַל תְּהִ֣י סָכָ֑ל” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.17).

items.claim: The deviation is licensed on a form claim the bytes refute — the verse does not carry the form-marker of the sayings zone it is being assimilated to — and the no-shared-token claim survives only under a token-level standard the cluster abandons elsewhere.
items.evidence: The row applies the sayings classification outside the designated zone on the ground that the verse is “of the same form as the sentence-zone sayings just before it”. That zone's byte marker is a verse-initial tov (12 openers book-wide, 7 in this chapter: 7:1, 7:2, 7:3, 7:5, 7:8, 7:11, 7:18; unit: verses). This verse opens “הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה תָּעֹ֣ז לֶחָכָ֑ם” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.19) and carries no tov token at all: the chapter-7 tov skeleton sweep returns 11 verses (7:1, 7:2, 7:3, 7:5, 7:8, 7:10, 7:11, 7:14, 7:18, 7:20, 7:26; unit: verses) and this verse is not among them. Its comparative is verbal with an intervening predicate — “מֵֽעֲשָׂרָה֙ שַׁלִּיטִ֔ים” (byte tier) governed by the preceding verb — not the nominal tov-X-min-Y construction of the zone's sayings. So the one piece of evidence carrying the deviation is byte-false, and the “bare comparative maxim” description conflates two different constructions. Second: “shares no content token with the moderation counsel before it” holds only at strict token identity. Under the root-level standard this cluster applies as binding evidence in its other rows, the wisdom root IS shared — “תִּתְחַכַּ֖ם” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.16) against “הַֽחָכְמָ֖ה” and “לֶחָכָ֑ם” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.19) — and this verse sits inside the chapter's wisdom chain (7 verses: 7:4, 7:10, 7:11, 7:12, 7:19, 7:23, 7:25; unit: verses), with the chain resuming at 7:23 and 7:25 just past the row's closing seam. The evidentiary standard shifts between rows with no byte-grounded discriminator offered.

items.claim: The ketiv/qere handling is byte-correct and properly disclosed, but the corollary argument rests on a below-byte-tier particle and an unquoted hinge verse, and the span's opening particle is treated opposite to the way the same cluster treats it two rows earlier.
items.evidence: Credit first: the quoted run “אֲשֶׁ֥ר גַּם את אַתָּ֖ה קִלַּ֥לְתָּ אֲחֵרִֽים” re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Eccl.7.22 and correctly carries the inline UNPOINTED ketiv immediately before its pointed qere; oshb:Eccl.7.22 is one of the 12 ketiv/qere notes (unit: verses) and the row discloses it as single-witness. The slicing hazard in a K/Q verse is handled properly. Challenge: the particle the row cites as the corollary marker for web:Eccl.7.21 re-collates at accent_stripped, NOT byte — the source form is “גַּ֤ם” (oshb:Eccl.7.21) — so a pointed run was hand-typed below quotation grade with no tier label, and that verse, the hinge of the whole corollary argument, carries no byte-tier quoted run anywhere in the row. The particle also carries no seam force in this chapter: the sweep returns 5 verses (7:6, 7:14, 7:18, 7:21, 7:22; unit: verses), none seam-aligned, and the row's own final verse carries 2 tokens of it. Second, the span opens on “כִּ֣י אָדָ֔ם אֵ֥ין צַדִּ֖יק בָּאָ֑רֶץ” (byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.20) — the same subordinating particle that the cluster's 7:11-7:12 row makes byte-grounded proof that a verse “does not stand alone without the claim it develops” (source form there “כִּ֛י”, byte tier, oshb:Eccl.7.12). Here it opens a span, with no byte-grounded discriminator between the two uses and no disclosure of a possible backward tie to 7:19. The righteous lexeme also straddles into this span — “צַדִּ֖יק” (byte tier) is the third of 3 chapter-7 sites (7:15, 7:16, 7:20; unit: verses), the first two in earlier rows of this cluster — undisclosed.
